A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EPiC work, with readable text, equations, tables and appendices. Some v2 figures overflow page boundaries, but their embedded image content is recoverable and supports comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original I2V evaluations on RealEstate10K and MiraData, Kubric-4D V2V results, and quantitative and qualitative ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical evaluations and adds baseline comparisons, backbone transfer, optical-flow robustness, training-scale experiments and failure cases.

M1.justification: Visibility-based anchor construction, artifact injection, masked Anchor-ControlNet outputs and point-cloud inference remain unchanged. The selected eight-layer, 256-dimensional adapter is retained in v1 Table 6 and v2 Table 7. The Wan experiment applies the framework to another backbone without specifying a new algorithmic component.

E1.justification: The core datasets and I2V/V2V tasks remain. v2 adds an explicit multi-camera scenario assessing consistency across multiple trajectories for one source video (Appendix G, Figure 20), plus compound-trajectory V2V examples. Movie clips and fine-grained regional control were already present in v1.

E2.justification: v2 Table 1 adds FloVD and Gen3C to I2V comparisons. Kubric-4D comparisons add TrajectoryCrafter and Gen3C beyond GCD. Figure 4's V2V comparison replaces ViewCrafter with TrajectoryCrafter, Gen3C and ReCamMaster while retaining GCD. These are evaluated comparators, although several were already cited in v1.

E3.justification: The stated Kubric sample count changes from 20 to 100. Added protocols include mixed-anchor training, Wan-14B evaluation, 30K training videos with 5K iterations, and full/easy-subset RealEstate10K PSNR. Reported efficiency budgets also change: AC3D moves from 10K to 750K steps, and EPiC's table batch size from 16 to 8, conflicting with v2's retained batch-16 implementation text. These revisions do not establish reruns.

E4.justification: v2 adds mixed-anchor and alignment-PSNR analysis, training-versus-inference mask ablations, alternative optical-flow estimators, backbone transfer, training-scale analysis and explicit failure cases (Table 3; Appendix D.4–D.8 and I). These investigate additional mechanisms and robustness questions beyond v1's retained ablations.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five fixed random seeds per test instance and report camera-metric means and standard deviations. Additional result rows use the existing practice; no new significance tests, confidence intervals or increased seed counts are reported.

E6.justification: Original Table 1 scores remain, but v2 adds comparator results and substantial new experimental outcomes. Examples include Wan quality score 84.24, EPiC full/easy-set PSNR 15.51/19.91, and scaled-training RE10K rotation error 0.34. These are newly reported settings, not same-setting improvements. New Figure 1 incorrectly labels Table 1's FloVD camera scores as EPiC.

T1.justification: The diffusion objective and camera-metric definitions remain equivalent. v2 rewrites the piecewise visibility-masked fusion as multiplication by a binary mask, without changing its mathematics. Neither version introduces theoretical propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The central aligned-anchor, lightweight adaptation and zero-shot V2V claims remain. v2 strengthens the introduction's efficiency claim from less than 10% to less than 5% of prior data and steps, adds a 15-GPU-hour claim, and promotes existing regional motion control into the contribution list.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations linking comparator failures to conditioning and full fine-tuning, clarifies camera-relative V2V control, and interprets the importance of training-time masking. Appendix I–J adds specific optical-flow, depth-estimation and occlusion failure boundaries beyond v1's predominantly backbone-dependent limitations.

D1.justification: v2 adds the 15-GPU-hour cost, identifies the Wan-2.1-I2V-14B-480P backbone, and clarifies V2V coordinate semantics. However, it removes v1 Appendix B's GCD checkpoint mode, maximum rotation and 256-by-384 evaluation-resizing details. Most original implementation hyperparameters and access information remain.

R1.justification: v2 adds references concerning camera estimation and optical flow, including Rockwell, Schonberger, GMFlow and UniMatch, while dropping several general video-control citations. It explicitly distinguishes its output masking from TrajectoryCrafter's latent-mask conditioning. The broader research positioning remains consistent.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, background and conclusion are substantially rewritten or condensed. Appendices are reorganized, Kubric results move into the main paper, and dedicated comparison and failure-analysis sections reshape the narrative. Author affiliations and citation style also change.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a two-column main layout, introduces an opening efficiency/performance chart, and relocates v1 Figure 1 to appendix Figure 6. Comparison tables and montages expand substantially, with new experimental displays. Several appendix montages overflow the page boundaries, clipping content and captions.

improvement.justification: Additional comparator evaluations, targeted robustness tests and explicit failure analysis better support EPiC's effectiveness and applicability. However, Figure 1 mislabels FloVD scores as EPiC, batch-size reports conflict, Kubric reproduction details disappear, and several figures are clipped. These reporting and presentation regressions limit the net benefit despite the stronger empirical examination.
